conditions.fixture: real written two-row-group nullable INT32 Parquet
conditions.timing: decode, scope cleanup and zero-used check; reference equality checked once per round

decision: Keep column-scoped admission: constant transient scratch and lower wide-schema peak justify measured CPU overhead. No new directory, parser callback, or configuration based on these results.
validation: All 9600 decodes complete, compare each variant against independently decoded Parquet metadata once per round, and assert zero budget usage after every decode.
limitations: Single local Node run; alternating order mitigates but does not eliminate JIT/GC/load effects
Narrow schemas show less memory benefit and a larger relative CPU cost
Fixed-width numeric schema benchmark does not establish all metadata shapes or whole-query speed
